newsitem.title: UK: Britain closes two meat plants over BSE.
newsitem.headline: Britain closes two meat plants over BSE.

text.p: Britain, trying to clean up its act after the mad cow fiasco, closed down two meat plants on Monday after investigations showed they were suspected of breaking a worldwide ban on exports of British beef.
The closures followed investigations by the Ministry of Agriculture and the European Commission's anti-fraud unit.

"Evidence is coming to light that some UK-based companies may have been exporting UK beef," Agriculture Minister Jack Cunningham said. "I am serving notices on two companies requiring them to stop the relevant business immediately."

"There is evidence, too, that the companies in question have been failing to comply with the basic requirements on record keeping, whose purpose is to ensure that the origins of meat can be traced, and falling down on hygiene standards," he added in a statement.
Earlier this month, the European Commission announced that hundreds of tonnes of beef had been exported from Britain to EU countries and nations outside the bloc.
The beef was fraudulently declared to be of Belgian origin. Britain reacted to the news by saying it had already launched an investigation into media allegations of illegal beef exports.
The new Labour government has, since coming to power on May 1, stepped up efforts to have the worldwide ban on British beef exports, imposed by the EU in March 1996, lifted.

"I am absolutely determined that the inquiries into this complex affair should be pursued to the end," Cunningham said. "I am determined to crack down hard on anyone who runs risks with public safety."
The EU clamped down on British beef exports after the London government said eating beef infected with BSE, or mad cow disease, could lead to people contracting a fatal brain disease, CJD.
